videos.title: US economic pressure will not force Iran to surrender, says Trita Parsi
videos.description: The Trump administration has announced "Operation Economic Outcast", a global campaign to sever Iran's economic lifelines. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called it "economic D-Day", warning that countries doing business with Tehran will face sanctions. But will this pressure force Iran to surrender, or trigger a dangerous escalation? In an interview with Al Jazeera, Trita Parsi, executive vice president of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, said the strategy is extremely unlikely to lead to the collapse or surrender of the Iranian government. He said the pattern so far has been that "when faced with either surrender or escalation, the Iranians escalate", adding that Iran still has "formidable escalatory options" and "escalation dominance." Parsi noted that 50 years of sanctions have imposed significant costs on Iran but have "not been able to translate that pain into desired change" in Iranian national security policies. He said the Trump administration has made "yet another miscalculation in a long series of massive miscalculations", warning that regime collapse could lead to civil war and regional instability. He concluded that the "most likely" outcome is "not an end to the conflict, but yet another round in the escalatory cycle between the two sides." videos.description: After nearly six months of war, the US appears to be taking a different approach to Iran.  President Donald Trump said Washington will carry out what he described as a 'crushing economic operation'.  Attempts to reach an agreement to end the war have stalled.  Now, the US is calling on other countries to join what it calls the greatest co-ordinated economic isolation in the history of the world.  For its part, Iran says that any countries joining the US campaign would be treated as enemies.  What does this mean for the conflict? videos.title: Trump has ‘run out of options’ in Iran war: Stephen Walt | The Bottom Line
videos.description: United States President Donald Trump’s unpredictability isn’t strengthening the US position in the Iran war, as “the Iranians have no reason to believe anything Trump tells them”, argues Stephen Walt, professor of international relations at Harvard University.  Walt tells host Steve Clemons that the war is now in a “hurting stalemate” where “neither side really wants to escalate; they’re just waiting for the other side to crack”.  On the Palestinian-Israeli front, Walt doesn’t see an opening for a genuine political solution, as neither US party is willing to exert pressure on Israel, where “there’s still a very strong commitment to 'Greater Israel'”.  #donaldtrump #israel #iran #unitedstates #uspolitics #palestine #politics #aljazeera #aljazeeraenglish
